reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Started with the official catalogue tree, course entries and programme-specific OER appendix. Recounted required credits by year and research component, checked progression, re-read the active workbook entries for the closest quantitative and physical-observation alternatives, then compared those findings with the finished decision and rendered-field mapping.
findings: 60 EC required. Optics, statistical physics, quantum mechanics and more mathematics underpin astronomy modules on stars, galaxies and observing techniques. Practical Astronomy precedes the observing lab. The current observing module expects calculus, optics, Python and introductory astrophysics.

30 EC approved free choice in the first semester, 6 EC Radiative Processes and 2 EC Research Skills & Scientific Integrity, and 22 EC research split into three assessed modules. Radiative Processes assumes prior classical electrodynamics and related physics.

OER appendix section 3.1 requires completing the first two years before the bachelor research project, with exceptions subject to authorization. The current research module describes a 20-week Leiden Observatory group project usually in pairs, subject to permission, with research, oral presentation and thesis credited separately.

Earth Observation uses satellite and drone imagery of Earth. Sustainability Essentials II supplies genuine waves and spectroscopy, and Image Processing & Computer Vision supplies calibration and feature analysis. The collective evidence supports preparatory and analogous capabilities while leaving astronomical observations, astrophysics and astronomical research without a progression. Both plans are feasible, so offering conflicts do not drive the disposition.
